recipes.name: 25 Minute Banh Mi Rice Bowls
recipes.protein_notes: 1.5 lb ground chicken or pork - commenters subbed mushrooms; crumbled tofu would also work with same sauce

ingredients.raw: 1 Serrano or jalapeÃ±o pepper, seeded and sliced

ingredients.item: mixed fresh herbs (cilantro, thai basil, mint)

ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons mixed sesame seeds and peanuts
1 1/2 pounds ground chicken or ground pork

recipes.notes: Site calories (530) given; macros estimated. Fish sauce makes sauce non-vegetarian; commenter subbed mushrooms for meat. Reviewers say sauce is salty (use low-sodium tamari) and real time is closer to 45 min.

recipes.file: Artichoke Tacos (Vegan Fish Tacos) - Forkful of Plants.mhtml
recipes.name: Artichoke Tacos (Vegan Fish Tacos)
recipes.protein_notes: artichokes are the star (low protein); page suggests firm tofu in same marinade/batter for higher protein, or hearts of palm

ingredients.raw: 1 tsp old bay seasoning or all purpose seasoning

ingredients.item: soft taco shells (wheat or corn tortillas)

ingredients.raw: cooking oil spray (optional, for crispier coating)

recipes.notes: Serving unit is per taco (makes 4 tacos). Use plain canned/frozen artichokes, not marinated. Gluten-free option: corn tortillas + GF panko. Air fryer 7-8 min works per comments.

recipes.file: Better Than Takeout Dan Dan Noodles. - Half Baked Harvest.mhtml
recipes.name: Better Than Takeout Dan Dan Noodles
recipes.protein_notes: 1/2 lb ground chicken or pork - author says double the mushrooms to make it vegetarian; crumbled tofu also an easy sub (use veg broth)

ingredients.raw: 6 cloves garlic, thinly sliced or smashed
1/4 cup hoisin sauce (make sure to use GF, if needed)
3 tablespoons creamy peanut butter or tahini
8 ounces Chinese style egg noodles, or rice noodles
ingredients.item: chinese egg noodles or rice noodles

ingredients.raw: 2 cups fresh baby spinach, roughly chopped

recipes.notes: Vegetarian: double mushrooms and use veg broth. Hoisin subs: soy sauce, miso paste. Keeps 2-3 days in fridge. Reviewers report longer than 30 min.
instructions: Make the chili oil: heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1/3 cup of the sesame oil, the garlic, and chili flakes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the garlic is fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and carefully transfer the oil to a heatproof bowl or jar.
Meanwhile, combine the soy sauce, hoisin sauce, honey, vinegar, peanut butter (or tahini), and 1/3 cup water in a bowl.

Cook the noodles according to package directions. Drain and set aside. To the same pot, add the broth and half of the soy sauce mixture. Bring to a simmer over medium heat and stir in the spinach. Keep warm.

Place the skillet used for the chili oil over medium-high heat. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons sesame oil and the chicken (or pork). Season with black pepper and brown all over, breaking it up as it cooks, about 5 minutes. Add the mushrooms and shallot and cook another 2-3 minutes. Slowly pour in the remaining soy sauce mixture, bring to a simmer, and cook until the sauce coats the meat and it begins to caramelize and crisp, about 5 minutes. Stir in 2-4 tablespoons of the chili oil. Remove from heat.
Ladle the broth into bowls, add the noodles, and toss to combine. Spoon the meat over the noodles and top with green onions and additional chili oil.

recipes.file: Big Green Fried Rice - Live Naturally Magazine.mhtml
recipes.name: Big Green Fried Rice
recipes.protein_notes: 2 eggs - modest protein; could add tofu or extra egg to boost

ingredients.raw: 4 green onions, white and green parts, chopped
1 cup sliced asparagus or green beans, trimmed and cut into 1/4-inch segments
1 tablespoon peeled and grated fresh ginger
2 cups well-chopped kale, trimmed and ribs removed
Chile-sesame oil and zest of 1 lemon to serve (optional)

recipes.notes: From Heidi Swanson's Super Natural Simple. Needs cold pre-cooked rice (make ahead). Very fast active cooking (~10 min).
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add green onions and asparagus and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until green onions soften.
Stir in garlic and ginger. Wait 30 seconds, then add rice and stir to separate the grains. Cook for about 3 minutes, until rice is hot, then stir in kale.
Shift rice and vegetables to the sides of the skillet and add remaining 1/2 tablespoon sesame oil to the pan. Add eggs and push them around until just set. Break up eggs with a spatula.
Drizzle in tamari and stir-fry everything together until well-combined, about 30 seconds.
To serve, drizzle with chile-sesame oil if you like a bit of heat and sprinkle with lemon zest. Serve immediately.

recipes.file: Broccoli Caesar with Smoky Tempeh Bits - alive magazine.mhtml
recipes.name: Broccoli Caesar with Smoky Tempeh Bits
recipes.protein_notes: 4 oz smoky crumbled tempeh plus cashew-butter dressing; more of a substantial vegetable course than a full main

ingredients.raw: 2 cloves garlic, grated with a microplane grater
1/2 tsp (2 mL) gluten-free tamari soy sauce

recipes.notes: Broccoli can be blanched (as written) or roasted at 400 F for ~20 min for a warm salad. Pairs well as a side or light main; add grain to bulk up.
instructions: To make the Creamy Cashew Caesar Dressing: in a jar with a tight-fitting lid, combine cashew butter, water, lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Stir until the cashew butter is broken up, mashing chunks against the sides of the jar to integrate it. Add garlic, Dijon mustard, capers, nutritional yeast, and olive oil. Tightly secure the lid and shake vigorously until the dressing is smooth and creamy. Set aside.

To make the salad: bring a large saucepan of water to a boil over medium-high heat. Add a fat pinch of salt and the broccoli florets, and simmer until the broccoli is just tender and bright green, about 4 minutes. Drain and run under cold water to stop the cooking. Set aside.
In a small bowl, stir together the paprika, smoked paprika, maple syrup, apple cider vinegar, and tamari. Set aside.

Dry the saucepan and return it to the stove over medium heat. Add the oil and let it heat until shimmering slightly. Add the crumbled tempeh, spreading it into a single layer. Let it sit and brown for a full 2 minutes, then stir and let sit for another minute. Pour the paprika mixture into the pan — it should sizzle. Stir to coat all of the tempeh, then remove from heat.

Place the broccoli on a serving platter. Drizzle the Creamy Cashew Caesar Dressing overtop. Scatter the smoky tempeh bits over as well. Garnish with nutritional yeast and freshly ground black pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.file: Charred Cauliflower Pitas with Halloumi and Harissa.mhtml
recipes.name: Charred Cauliflower Pitas with Halloumi and Harissa
recipes.protein_notes: broiled halloumi slices; could sub grilled tofu for vegan

ingredients.raw: Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
8 ounces halloumi cheese, sliced widthwise into 1/4-inch-thick pieces

recipes.notes: Uses broiler for cauliflower and halloumi. Store-bought harissa works. Serve with extra harissa on the side. Roughly 30 min total.

recipes.file: Chickpea Salad Sandwich Recipe - Love and Lemons.mhtml
recipes.name: Chickpea Salad Sandwich
recipes.protein_notes: mashed chickpea 'tuna' salad with tahini; fully plant-based

ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups cooked chickpeas, drained and rinsed
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
handful of thin green beans, trimmed
8 to 10 Kalamata olives, pitted and sliced in half
thinly sliced red onion, rinsed and dried
vegan mayo (or regular mayo), for spreading

recipes.notes: Vegan pan bagnat spin. Chickpea mixture keeps 3 days in fridge. Veggies are flexible. 1.5 cups chickpeas = one can. Use a soft baguette.
instructions: Make the chickpea salad: in a food processor, combine the chickpeas, tahini, Dijon mustard, garlic, capers, green onion, cilantro, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Pulse until combined but not pureed. Season to taste.
Blanch the green beans: boil in salted water 1½ minutes, then transfer to an ice water bath to stop cooking. Drain, pat dry, and chop into 1-inch pieces.

Assemble the sandwiches: spread the chickpea salad on one side of the baguette. Press the green beans into the chickpea salad and top with the olives and red onion. Spread mayo on the other half and top with cucumber, radish, and basil. Season with salt and pepper, press together, slice, and serve.

recipes.file: Creamy Coconut-Lime Rice With Peanuts Recipe.mhtml
recipes.name: Creamy Coconut-Lime Rice With Peanuts
recipes.protein_notes: peanuts + peanut butter; page suggests topping with fried eggs to make it a fuller main

ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup roasted and salted peanuts, crushed
2 cups ripe cherry tomatoes, halved (about 10 ounces)
1 cup roughly chopped mixed herbs (such as dill, cilantro or mint)

recipes.notes: All plant-based. Serve at room temperature the day it's made. Commenters sub mango for tomatoes, cashews for peanuts; can top with fried or hard-boiled eggs for extra protein.
instructions: Cook the rice according to the packaging instructions until tender, replacing 1 1/4 cups of the cooking water with 1 1/4 cups of the coconut milk. Fluff the cooked rice with a fork, transfer to a serving bowl, season with salt and pepper (it should taste well-seasoned and almost buttery), and let cool.

While the rice is cooking, add 1/4 cup coconut milk to another bowl. Finely grate the ginger and garlic into the bowl, followed by the zest of 1 lime. Juice both limes into the bowl. Whisk in 1/4 cup of the peanuts, the peanut butter, sugar, and sambal, and season with salt.

When ready to serve, add the tomatoes and 3/4 cup of the herbs to the bowl with the rice. Pour in the coconut dressing, toss well to coat, season with pepper, and top with the remaining 1/4 cup crushed peanuts and 1/4 cup herbs. For the best flavor, serve at room temperature the day it is made.

recipes.file: Crispy Gnocchi With Sausage and Broccoli Recipe.mhtml
recipes.name: Crispy Gnocchi With Sausage and Broccoli
recipes.protein_notes: Italian sausage pinched into meatballs - could sub veggie sausage (a commenter made it vegan with Beyond sausage and vegan parm)

ingredients.raw: 1 large head broccoli (about 1 pound), florets cut into 1 1/2- to 2-inch pieces, stems thinly sliced
1 pound hot or sweet Italian sausage, casings removed
1/4 cup grated Parmesan, plus more for serving

recipes.notes: Gnocchi go on the pan uncooked. Easily vegetarian/vegan with plant-based sausage and parm.

recipes.file: Easy Lentil and Halloumi Curry - Easy Cheesy Vegetarian.mhtml
recipes.name: Easy Lentil and Halloumi Curry
recipes.protein_notes: brown lentils plus fried halloumi; page suggests paneer as a halloumi sub

ingredients.raw: 225 g (~8 oz / 1 small block) halloumi cheese, cut into bitesize pieces

recipes.notes: Vegetables are flexible (peppers, eggplant, carrots, cauliflower, peas all work). Serve with rice or naan, cilantro, and yogurt/raita.

recipes.file: french onion baked lentils and farro â€“ smitten kitchen.mhtml
recipes.name: French Onion Baked Lentils and Farro
recipes.protein_notes: Lentils and farro provide plant protein; gruyere cheese adds significant dairy protein

ingredients.raw: 2 pounds (910 grams) yellow onions (4 large or 5 medium), sliced
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
2 tablespoons (30 ml) dry sherry, vermouth, or white wine (optional)
ingredients.item: dry sherry, vermouth, or white wine

ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup (135 grams) dried lentils, green (le puy) or brown (italian)
A few sprigs of fresh thyme
6 cups (1.4 liters) vegetable broth + splashes more, if needed
2 cups (8 ounces or 225 grams) coarsely grated gruyere cheese

recipes.notes: Serves 6 to 8. Gluten-free option: sub shortgrain brown rice for farro. Keeps 4-5 days in fridge; base can be made ahead and cheese broiled before serving.
instructions: Caramelize the onions: heat butter and olive oil in a large, deep saute pan (ovenproof if you have one) over medium heat. Add the onions, toss to coat, and cover. Reduce heat to medium-low and let steep 15-20 minutes. Uncover, raise heat to medium-high, stir in about 2 tsp kosher salt, and cook, stirring every few minutes, until brown, soft, and sweet, about 20 minutes more, reducing heat to medium once their liquid cooks off.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C).

Assemble the casserole: add garlic to the onions and cook, stirring, 1 minute. Add the sherry (if using) and cook until it disappears. Add the farro and cook 2 minutes. Add the lentils, 6 cups broth, and thyme, and bring to a simmer. Season well with salt and pepper. If your pan isn't ovenproof, transfer to a casserole dish.

Bake, covered, stirring about halfway through, until the lentils and farro are tender, 40-50 minutes. If the liquid absorbs before then, add another 1/4-1/2 cup broth — aim for a risotto-like looseness. Fish out the thyme stems.
Sprinkle with gruyere and broil until browned on top.

recipes.file: Kale Power Salad with Spicy Almond Dressing _ The First Mess.mhtml
recipes.name: Kale Power Salad with Spicy Almond Dressing
recipes.protein_notes: Crispy baked spiced tofu bits plus almonds in the dressing and as garnish

ingredients.raw: 1/2 cup sliced almonds, soaked for 1 hour and drained (dressing)
2 medium sweet potatoes (about 500 grams), peeled and diced
1 350 gram block firm OR extra firm tofu, drained and torn
1 ripe avocado, peeled, pitted and chopped

recipes.notes: Serves 4-6. Sunflower seeds or cashews can sub for almonds. Dressing is great doubled for grain bowls. Requires a blender.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.

Make the spicy almond dressing: in a blender, combine the almonds, garlic, nutritional yeast, water, olive oil, white wine vinegar, lime juice, tamari, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, hot sauce, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth and creamy, adding a splash more water if too thick. Taste and adjust seasoning; set aside.

Make a spice blend: stir together the nutritional yeast, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and chili powder. Put the sweet potatoes in one bowl and the tofu in another; blot the tofu very dry with a clean towel first.

Divide the spice blend between the sweet potatoes and tofu. Drizzle both with olive oil (1½ tbsp each) and season with salt and pepper. Add the arrowroot and cornmeal to the tofu only, then toss each until evenly coated.

Spread the sweet potatoes and tofu on opposite sides of the baking sheet, giving each piece space. Roast 35 minutes, stirring/flipping halfway, until the sweet potatoes are tender and the tofu is crunchy outside.
Combine the kale with the remaining tablespoon of olive oil, lime juice, maple syrup, salt, and pepper in a large bowl. Massage with your hands until slightly tenderized, about 1 minute.

Drizzle the kale with some of the dressing, then top with the roasted sweet potatoes, tofu, avocado, and red onion. Drizzle with more dressing and finish with the toasted sliced almonds. Serve immediately.

recipes.file: One-Pot Beans, Greens and Grains Recipe.mhtml
recipes.name: One-Pot Beans, Greens and Grains
recipes.protein_notes: One can of any beans plus quinoa; optional egg/cheese/nut toppings add more protein

ingredients.raw: 1 cup quinoa, long-grain white rice or a mix of the two, rinsed
1 bunch collard greens, kale, spinach or other hearty dark leafy green
ingredients.item: collard greens, kale, or other dark leafy greens

ingredients.raw: Toppings (optional): toasted nuts or seeds, fresh herbs, cheese, soft-boiled egg, avocado, hot sauce
ingredients.item: optional toppings (nuts, herbs, cheese, egg, avocado, hot sauce)

recipes.notes: Extremely flexible template: any beans, any hearty greens, quinoa/rice/other grains. Good warm or cold, works for grain-bowl lunches.

recipes.file: Roasted Broccoli and Tofu Bowls with Peanut Sauce â€¢.mhtml
recipes.name: Roasted Broccoli and Tofu Bowls with Peanut Sauce
recipes.protein_notes: Marinated baked extra-firm tofu plus peanut butter sauce and optional peanut garnish

ingredients.raw: 1 block (12-16 oz) extra-firm or super firm tofu
1 TBSP fresh ginger, grated (or 1 tsp dry ginger powder)
1 red bell pepper, chopped into 1-inch pieces
1 cup carrots, zucchini, or other vegetables (optional)
garnish: chopped peanuts, cilantro, sesame seeds, green onions, chili garlic sauce (optional)
ingredients.item: garnishes (peanuts, cilantro, sesame seeds, green onions)

recipes.notes: Tofu can marinate 10 minutes up to several days. Frozen broccoli works without thawing. Doubling the peanut sauce is recommended.
instructions: Start by marinating the tofu. Press the tofu if desired, then cut into small cubes. Stir the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, and ginger together in a medium bowl. Toss the tofu in the marinade gently and let sit for at least 10 minutes (up to several days in the fridge).

While the tofu sits, start cooking the rice: bring a pot of water to a boil, add the rice, and boil (about 30 minutes for brown rice, about 10 for white), then drain. Pour it back in the pot, cover, and keep warm.

Preheat the oven to 400F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Arrange the broccoli, bell pepper, sweet potato, and any other vegetables on the sheet. Spray lightly with olive oil if desired, and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Bake 25-30 minutes, tossing halfway through, until golden brown and tender.
After the tofu has marinated at least 10 minutes, pour it onto a separate baking sheet in an even layer and bake alongside the vegetables for 25-30 minutes, tossing halfway, until golden brown.
Meanwhile, make the peanut sauce by stirring all the sauce ingredients together in a small jar or measuring cup (or blend together), adding hot water a tablespoon at a time if it needs thinning.

To serve, arrange bowls of rice, vegetables, and tofu. Drizzle peanut sauce liberally over everything, and top with cilantro, crushed peanuts, sliced green onions, sesame seeds, and/or chili garlic sauce.

recipes.file: Romanesco Glow Salad â€” Luna Yoga Montreal _ Yoga Classes, Jivamukti, Yoga Flo, Teacher Training.mhtml
recipes.name: Meyer Lemon Romanesco Glow Salad
recipes.protein_notes: Walnuts are the only notable protein source; this is a light side-style salad

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons grapeseed or other neutral-flavoured oil (dressing)
1 medium head Romanesco broccoli (or cauliflower), broken up into florets
1 medium sweet apple, cored and chopped
1/3 cup walnut halves, toasted and chopped

recipes.notes: Romanesco is blitzed in a food processor to couscous texture. Keeps refrigerated up to 3 days. Light on protein â€” best as a side or paired with a protein.
instructions: Make the dressing: in a small bowl, whisk together the Meyer lemon zest, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, grapeseed oil, salt, and pepper until combined. Set aside.
Make the salad: working in batches, pulse the Romanesco florets in a food processor until couscous-like in size and texture. Transfer to a large bowl.
Add the apple, celery, grapes, green onions, sage, and walnuts to the bowl. Season with salt and pepper and toss to combine.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss. Serve immediately, or store in the fridge up to 3 days.

recipes.file: Sheet Pan Ratatouille with Crispy Baked Tofu - Minimalist Baker Recipes.mhtml
recipes.name: Sheet Pan Ratatouille with Crispy Baked Tofu
recipes.protein_notes: Crispy Baked Italian Herb Tofu (separate linked sub-recipe, 1 batch) provides the protein

1/2 medium red bell pepper, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1 Tbsp dried Italian herbs (or sub dried oregano + basil)
1 batch Crispy Baked Tofu with Italian Herbs (14 oz firm tofu + herbs)
Creamy Pesto Sauce (vegan pesto + cashews or store-bought)
Pasta, polenta, or grain of choice (optional)
ingredients.item: pasta, polenta, or grain of choice

recipes.notes: Requires two linked sub-recipes (Crispy Baked Italian Herb Tofu, Creamy Pesto Sauce). Freezer friendly 1 month; keeps 3-4 days.

recipes.file: Sheet-Pan Baked Feta With Broccolini, Tomatoes and Lemon Recipe.mhtml
recipes.name: Sheet-Pan Baked Feta With Broccolini, Tomatoes and Lemon
recipes.protein_notes: Two 6-8 oz blocks of feta roasted with vegetables; commenters say one block is plenty

ingredients.raw: 1 bunch broccolini, ends trimmed, or broccoli
1 small red onion, peeled, quartered and cut into wedges
1 lemon, 1/2 cut into thin rounds, 1/2 for serving
3 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for serving
2 (6- to 8-ounce) blocks feta, cut into 1-inch slices
Cooked orzo or farro, for serving
1/2 cup fresh basil or cilantro leaves, roughly chopped (optional)

recipes.notes: Broccoli can substitute for broccolini. Serve over orzo or farro. Several commenters use only one block of feta. Best served hot.

recipes.file: Sweet Chile Grain Bowl With Tofu Recipe.mhtml
recipes.name: Sweet Chile Grain Bowl With Tofu
recipes.protein_notes: One 14-16 oz package firm/extra-firm tofu, pressed and roasted with chile-crisp sauce

ingredients.raw: 1 (14- to 16-ounce) package firm or extra-firm tofu
1/4 cup neutral oil, such as grapeseed
1 1/2 tablespoons fish sauce (or substitute Yondu, coconut aminos, or more soy sauce)
1 tablespoon chile crisp, more to taste
1 1/2 pounds napa cabbage, halved lengthwise, cored and sliced
4 cups cooked grains (rice, farro, barley, millet) or salad greens
ingredients.item: cooked grains (rice, farro, barley, or millet)

recipes.notes: Contains fish sauce as written; recipe offers subs (Yondu, coconut aminos, or more soy sauce) to make it plant-based. Nutrition likely excludes the grains.
instructions: Heat oven to 425F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Cut the tofu into 1-inch-thick slabs. Cut each slab in half to make squares. Line a plate or baking sheet with paper towels and place tofu on top. Place another layer of paper towels on the tofu and weigh down with a skillet or cans. Let sit for at least 15 minutes.

While the tofu is draining, make the sauce: heat the oil in a small pot or skillet over medium-high. Stir in the garlic and let cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Whisk in ketchup, soy sauce, fish sauce, 1/2 tablespoon of the chile crisp, and the rice vinegar. Set aside to cool for a few minutes.
In a small bowl, mix together the tomatoes, the remaining 1/2 tablespoon chile crisp, and a pinch of salt. Set aside.
Place tofu on one side of the prepared baking sheet and generously brush both sides of the pieces with the sauce.
Add the cabbage to a bowl, sprinkle lightly with salt, and toss with 1/4 cup sauce (reserve remaining sauce for serving). Spread cabbage on the other side of the baking sheet in an even layer.

Roast tofu and cabbage for about 30 minutes, tossing the cabbage after 15 minutes. The tofu should be lightly golden at the edges and the cabbage tender and bronzed. Toss about half of the scallions into the cabbage and squeeze lime wedges over everything (or drizzle with a little rice vinegar). Taste cabbage and add more salt or sauce, if needed.

To serve, put 1 cup grains in each of 4 bowls. Drizzle the grains with a little of the sauce. Top with tofu, cabbage, and spicy tomatoes. Garnish with cilantro and remaining scallions, and drizzle with remaining sauce. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Telegraph Rainbow Salad
recipes.protein_notes: Kidney beans and chickpeas plus tahini and sunflower seeds; mixed plant proteins

ingredients.raw: 4-5 handfuls of baby romaine or Little Gem lettuce
ingredients.item: baby romaine or little gem lettuce

ingredients.raw: 1 carrot, scrubbed and sliced into thin coins
Big handful of whole grain croutons or crumbled Lemon-Garlic Pita Chips
ingredients.item: whole grain croutons or pita chips

ingredients.raw: 1/3 c toasted sunflower seeds, to serve

recipes.notes: Meal-size loaded salad with orange-tahini-ponzu dressing (leftover dressing keeps 5 days refrigerated). Sub maple syrup for honey to veganize.

recipes.name: Barley Bowls with Chickpeas, Roasted Vegetables & Avocado Dressing
recipes.protein_notes: chickpeas plus barley; fully plant-based

ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil (for the bowls)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste (for the bowls)
3 cups Crispy Chickpeas (page 198) or store-bought, such as Saffron Road brand
1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil (for the dressing)
3 tablespoons white wine vinegar or distilled white vinegar
1/2 teaspoon honey or agave for vegans
2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice (from 1/2 medium lemon)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste (for the dressing)

recipes.notes: From The Weekday Vegetarians by Jenny Rosenstrach, p.49. The book's Crispy Chickpeas (p.198) and Pickled Onions (p.231) component recipes were converted to plain chickpeas and sliced red onion for the grocery list, per household preference. Times are estimated (not listed in the source).
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425F.

Prepare the bowls: in a medium pot, combine the barley and 3 cups water. Bring to a boil, then decrease the heat to low and keep at the laziest simmer. Cover and cook, checking for doneness after 30 minutes. You want the grains to be tripled in size and tender but not mushy. If there is still water left in the pot when they've reached this point (you might have to let them cook another 5 to 10 minutes), strain the barley in a colander, the way you'd strain pasta.

Meanwhile, in a large bowl, toss together the Brussels sprouts, broccoli, olive oil, and some salt and pepper. Spread them out in an even layer on a sheet pan and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until everything is crispy and browned.

Make the dressing: meanwhile, in a small food processor, whirl together the avocado, olive oil, vinegar, honey, lemon juice, 2 tablespoons water, and some salt and pepper. The final consistency should be thin enough to drizzle, so add more water as necessary. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Divide the barley evenly among four bowls and top with the roasted vegetables, chickpeas, and sliced red onion. Drizzle with avocado dressing and serve.

recipes.name: Rigatoni with Honeynut Squash, Chard & Hazelnuts
recipes.protein_notes: 1/2 cup grated Parmesan (about 2 oz) tossed into the pasta; 1/3 cup toasted hazelnuts add secondary protein/crunch.

ingredients.raw: 2 small honeynut squash (about 3 pounds total), peeled, halved, seeded, and cut into 1/2-inch cubes (6 to 7 cups)
Freshly ground black pepper to taste
1 pound rigatoni or tube pasta of your choice—just don't use noodles
5 cups roughly chopped Swiss chard (including stems), amaranth, kale, or spinach
1/3 cup crushed or roughly chopped toasted hazelnuts (see page 237 for crushing tips)

recipes.notes: From The Weekday Vegetarians by Jenny Rosenstrach, p.84. Times are estimated (not listed in the source).
instructions: Preheat the oven to 425F. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.

Combine the squash and onion on the prepared sheet pan and drizzle with 3 tablespoons of the olive oil. Sprinkle with red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper, and using your hands, toss until every piece is coated and shiny. Roast until the squash looks crispy around the edges, 20 to 25 minutes.

Meanwhile, when the salted water comes to a boil, cook the rigatoni according to the package directions until it's al dente. Reserve about 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain the pasta and immediately toss it right in the strainer with 1 tablespoon of the butter.

Set the pasta back on the stovetop over low heat. Add the remaining 2 tablespoons butter, the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, and the garlic. Cook until the garlic is golden, about 1 minute, then add the chard, salt, and black pepper, tossing until the chard has softened and wilted, about 2 minutes. Toss in the rigatoni along with the Parmesan, more salt and black pepper, and about 1/4 cup of the reserved pasta water to help distribute the cheese and make the pasta saucy. (Add more pasta water, a tablespoon at a time, as needed.) Toss in the squash-onion mixture, then serve in bowls topped with hazelnuts.

recipes.name: A Farrotto for All Seasons
recipes.protein_notes: Farro is the base grain (no protein-enum category for grains); 1/3 cup grated Parmesan is the only distinct protein-labeled ingredient. Book also suggests topping with a Seven-Minute Egg (separate recipe, p.197) for more protein.

ingredients.raw: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
Dash of dried red pepper flakes
4 cups vegetable stock, store-bought or homemade (page 232), warmed
Summer add-in: 1 cup quartered cherry tomatoes
Summer add-in: uncooked kernels from 2 medium ears of corn
Summer add-in: chopped fresh basil, to finish

recipes.notes: From The Weekday Vegetarians by Jenny Rosenstrach, p.50. This is a seasonal template recipe — the book offers different vegetable add-ins by season. Defaulted here to the Summer add-in (cherry tomatoes, corn, basil) since that's what's in season now; the book's other variants (Fall: roasted honeynut squash with crispy sage; Winter: roasted Brussels sprouts and peas; Spring: sauteed mushrooms and asparagus) can be swapped in later on request. Times are estimated except the farro's stated 30-35 minute cook window.
instructions: Combine the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of the butter in a deep medium-size skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes and cook until the onion is softened, stirring occasionally, about 3 minutes.

Stir in the farro and wine and increase the heat to medium-high. Stir until most of the wine has been absorbed, then start adding vegetable stock in 1-cup drizzles, adding more as the liquid is absorbed. (You want the grains to always be just slightly submerged.) This is when you should prepare your seasonal vegetable add-in.

When the farro is cooked (porridge but still a little toothy, like risotto, 30 to 35 minutes), turn off the heat and stir in the remaining tablespoon butter, the Parmesan, and the desired vegetable combination.
Summer add-in: toss in 1 cup quartered cherry tomatoes and the uncooked kernels from 2 medium ears of corn. Serve the farrotto in bowls topped with chopped fresh basil.

recipes.name: Spicy-Tangy-Smoky Pinto Bean Bowls
recipes.protein_notes: 3 cups (or two 15-oz cans) pinto beans are the entire protein base; fully plant-based unless dairy toppings (sour cream, cheddar) are added.

ingredients.raw: 3 tablespoons neutral oil (such as canola or vegetable, or extra-virgin olive oil in a pinch)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
3 cups cooked pinto beans, or 2 (15-ounce) cans, rinsed and drained
1/2 cup water (or reserved bean cooking liquid if you home-cooked your beans)
ingredients.item: water or reserved bean cooking liquid

ingredients.raw: 4 cups cooked rice (any kind), for serving

Optional toppings: guacamole, sour cream (omit for vegans), cilantro, shredded lettuce tossed with oil and red wine vinegar, shredded sharp cheddar cheese (omit for vegans), sliced radishes, Salsa Fresca, minced red onion

recipes.notes: From The Weekday Vegetarians by Jenny Rosenstrach, pp.52-53.
instructions: In a medium pot set over medium heat, combine the oil, onion, salt, and black pepper and cook until the onion is soft, about 3 minutes.
Add the garlic, paprika, tomato paste, and cayenne (if using), stirring everything together and allowing the tomato paste to sizzle and toast.
Toss in the beans and 1/2 cup water (or bean cooking liquid if you home-cooked your beans) and heat until everything has warmed through, 5 to 6 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the vinegar. (The beans should be slightly stewy; if they aren't, add a little more water to loosen them up.) Serve with cooked rice and your desired toppings.
